title: Build Scripts and Custom Build Steps knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Build Scripts and Custom Build Steps”?
options: Rust tooling makes the build, dependency graph, formatting, linting, and test steps repeatable. Use the project’s declared toolchain and Cargo metadata rather than relying on undocumented local state.
Rust automatically verifies every runtime, network, and business rule without tests.
The topic removes the need to read compiler diagnostics or library documentation.
The topic requires replacing all standard-library APIs with third-party packages.
questions.answer_key: Rust tooling makes the build, dependency graph, formatting, linting, and test steps repeatable. Use the project’s declared toolchain and Cargo metadata rather than relying on undocumented local state.
questions.explanation: Rust tooling makes the build, dependency graph, formatting, linting, and test steps repeatable. Use the project’s declared toolchain and Cargo metadata rather than relying on undocumented local state. The other choices overstate language guarantees or recommend unrelated practices.

questions.prompt: What is the most dependable way to apply “Build Scripts and Custom Build Steps” in a new program?
options: Start with a minimal example, state its assumptions, verify the expected behavior, and test a relevant boundary case.
Change several unrelated implementation details until the output looks plausible.
Ignore warnings and errors if the program appears to work once.
Use nightly-only features by default even when stable Rust is sufficient.
questions.answer_key: Start with a minimal example, state its assumptions, verify the expected behavior, and test a relevant boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproductions and explicit boundary tests make the behavior easier to verify and maintain.

questions.prompt: When a result involving “Build Scripts and Custom Build Steps” differs from your prediction, what should you do first?
options: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and full diagnostic/error, check the supported toolchain or dependency, and retry one change at a time.
Suppress the error without investigating it.
Assume the compiler is wrong and disable checks globally.
Add an unrelated dependency before reproducing the issue.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the case, inspect the inputs and full diagnostic/error, check the supported toolchain or dependency, and retry one change at a time.
questions.explanation: A reproducible failure and precise diagnostic are the best starting points for debugging.
